label: De ente extrinsic-source controls: five premise omissions and one nonvacuity case
paraphrase: Closed finite controls on interpretations over Bool (two beings, two principles, one respect), in each of which false actually exists with esse distinct from its essence. (1) Brute esse: nothing causes anything and nothing is from its nature; the literal De ente disjunction, the weak exhaustiveness, some-cause and the other-cause conclusion fail while the self-causation reading, no-self-causation, actuality of causes of being and the efficiency bridge hold. (2) Formal nature: false's esse is from its nature (NATURE_SOURCE_1) but not efficiently caused by its quiddity, and nothing causes anything; the literal disjunction, self-causation reading, no-self-causation and actuality of causes of being hold, while the efficiency bridge, weak exhaustiveness, some-cause and conclusion fail. 'Formal' is a label: fromNature is an unconstrained primitive, so this shows that the two nature senses are independent, not a model of formal causation. (3) Self-cause: false causes its own esse; only no-self-causation fails among the inputs, and the conclusion fails. (4) Unrealized quiddity: false's quiddity efficiently causes its esse without false causing it; the self-causation reading and some-cause fail, and the conclusion fails. (5) Nonactual cause: true, not in act, causes false's esse; only actuality of causes of being fails, and the conclusion fails. (6) Nonvacuity: every input holds and true, in act, causes false's esse. Statements about these interpretations only: they show which premises the conclusion needs, not that brute or formally sourced esse is possible or plausible.
